summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (porting the node/v3 model to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack with grant-root awareness) end-to-end via the GSD workflow: research, plan, verify, then wave-based parallel execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed and 13 of an eventually-18-plan set were merged and green (full crates/core + crates/sdk read/rotation/seal/emit/write-owner foundation), but the FUSE consumer cutover (69-09) hit three successive architectural blockers requiring incremental re-scoping (write-plane emit API, then write-owner tree materialization); it is now being executed as a bounded multi-slice 'grind' (Slice 1 done, Slice 2 launching) gated on a real E2E run rather than compile-green.

repo: GSD's commit helper reports a false 'commit_failed' even when the commit actually lands cleanly (lint-staged completes but the wrapper still reports failure) — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry the commit.

Worktree-isolated executors sometimes mis-report their own `expected_base` as their last docs commit rather than the true fork point — verify via `git merge-base <worktree-branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.

Running `cargo fmt` on a crate's `lib.rs` follows `mod` declarations and reformats the whole crate, including unrelated pre-existing drifted files — executors must scope-check `git diff --stat` and revert out-of-scope reformats before committing.

Fresh git worktrees lack `node_modules`, so the husky pre-commit `lint-staged` hook fails on the first commit attempt; fix with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, or use `--no-verify` when the change is pure Rust untouched by lint-staged.

`ApiNodeFetcher` (crates/sdk) is a borrow adapter (`{ api: &'a ApiClient }`) with no `::new` constructor — it must be constructed inline at each read-path call site, not stored as a field (storing it beside owned `Arc<ApiClient>` would be self-referential).

The FUSE mount is a read-WRITE vault owner (signs IPNS records, seals new children under each parent's key) unlike the TS Phase 68.2 web mirror which is read-only — so `InodeKind` must carry read_key + write_key + ipns_private_key per node, not just a read key.

The gated read listing (`ResolvedChild`/`list_folder`) unseals a child's read key only to immediately zeroize it and never touches the write-body — it cannot supply key material for a read-write owner; a separate `list_folder_owned`/`ResolvedOwnedChild` API (69-17) was needed.

The current `JournalOp` write/replay wire format (crates/sdk/src/queue.rs) is hex-string fields under user-ECIES-under-self.public_key — structurally unrelated to node/v3 symmetric parent-key sealing, requiring its own reshape (69-18) before the FUSE write path can emit Node/v3.

The orchestrator's own working directory (`cipher-box-phase69`) is itself a linked git worktree of the main `cipher-box` repo, and executor worktrees resolve under `cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/` — manifests must pin `orchestrator_root` correctly.

code.finding: Original research cited a `JournalOp::MkdirPublish.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` cross-crate weld as the key landmine forcing atomicity — this field does not exist on the live tree; the actual weld only appears in fuse-side `MkdirJournalResult` (journal_helpers.rs:97), invalidating that part of the original design.
InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} store ipns_private_key + folder_key/file_key for signing — a read-write owner model with no write_key plane prior to the Phase 69 grind's Slice 1 reshape.

list_folder_owned(fetcher, high_water, ipns_name, folder_read_key, folder_write_key) -> Vec<ResolvedOwnedChild> — added by plan 69-17 to recover per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} through the same SC#6 gate as list_folder, enabling write-owner materialization for the FUSE mount.
seal_node only seals the read-body; seal_published_node (added in 69-15) seals both read and write bodies, populating PublishedNode.write_sealed which was previously never set.

workflow: Canary-testing the very first plan of a wave synchronously (not fanned out) validates the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline before committing to parallel dispatch — worth the extra round trip on a new/risky pipeline.
Durable scratchpad handoff files plus ScheduleWakeup let planning/execution state survive both an explicit user pause and later context compaction without losing recovery state.

When a subagent halts with an architectural blocker instead of forcing broken code, independently re-verify its grounding claims (grep counts, blast-radius numbers) against the live tree before accepting or relaying them to the user — subagent estimates can be stale or overstated.

When a plan proves too large for one autonomous executor session to reach a compiling boundary, decompose it into a committed 'grind runbook' defining the frozen target shape, then dispatch bounded per-slice executors on the same branch (accepting intermediate RED) rather than repeatedly re-attempting the whole plan atomically.
Distinguish a session/usage-limit death (zero edits made, generic API error) from a genuine architectural blocker before reacting — the former just needs a wait-and-retry, not a re-scope.

friction: gsd-planner suffered an API crash mid-run during initial phase planning, leaving 13/14 plans written and requiring filesystem-fallback recovery.
A worktree executor for 69-16 stalled mid-stream on an API error, leaving uncommitted work that had to be manually inspected, finished, and committed by the orchestrator.
The 69-09 atomic FUSE cutover executor died from an account session-limit error mid-exploration (no architectural cause), requiring a wait-for-reset and re-dispatch.

Three successive in-execution architectural discoveries (missing write-path Node emission, missing write-plane emit API, missing write-owner tree materialization) were not caught by the upfront research/planning gates, each forcing a stop-research-replan cycle before execution could proceed.
GSD's commit-status reporting produced a false 'commit_failed' on essentially every commit in this session, requiring manual git log verification each time.
A scratchpad handoff write used a mistakenly doubled path segment ('phase69-phase69'), requiring a follow-up move to the correct location.
Working directory (cwd) drifted mid-session, causing a commit command to fail until absolute paths were used.
open_items: 69-09 atomic FUSE flip is mid-grind: Slice 1 (InodeKind reshape + CipherBoxFS wiring) is done and committed on the combined 69-18 branch; Slices 2 (read path), 3 (write path), 4 (replay.rs), and 5 (glue/desktop/SC#6 CI gate) remain before reaching cargo-green.
Final merge of 69-18+69-09 is gated on a real local sdk-e2e + desktop-e2e (docker + TEE) run per user decision, not just cargo check --workspace — this run has not yet happened.
69-10 (delete legacy crates/core types, D-04) and 69-13 (grant-gated write path + SC#2 + D-07) remain unexecuted, blocked behind 69-09.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration + TEST-03, autonomous:false) is deliberately deferred as a hand-off to the user's Windows machine.
Plan-checker earlier flagged that the SC#6 grep-gate in 69-06/69-09 uses a placeholder symbol name that must be confirmed against the real crate-private resolve symbol at execution/build time.

69-14's correction of the desktop E2E GitHub Actions workflow name (actual name is 'Desktop E2E Tests', not 'CI E2E Tests' as ROADMAP/CONTEXT word it) should be double-checked when that plan executes.
